## Deviations from the run prompt (all deliberate, all verified)

1. **No scaffold zip exists** (searched the project and Downloads); the folder was created with the §6 layout.
2. **"New data" adds no new forecastable series.** Compute Atlas, the EU EED report and AWARE 2.0 are cross-sections; the only monthly series are Ember electricity and CO2 intensity, which Co-RE's cached run already covers for the same US / India / Europe zones. So old-vs-new collapses to one Ember series set, forecast at two grains: dcfootprint (Ember zones + regional aggregate; EU-27 only) and Co-RE (95 zones incl. non-EU Europe; 24 G3P water basins).
3. **xLSTM, TimesFM 2.5, Chronos-2 were not re-run**: their fresh run on the same series would reproduce the cache. The cache was re-scored with this run's metric set; its per-zone RMSE reproduces Co-RE's own `model_comparison_region.csv` exactly (856/856 zone-model pairs, max abs diff 0.0).
4. **Real Nexus not run.** One gemma4:26b call via Ollama took 534 s on this CPU (3,985 tokens, ~8.6 tok/s, visible answer empty after the thinking tokens). The notebook's 5 agents x N_SPLITS=6 per series put the country-level run alone at days of compute; the 95-zone run far longer. Needs a GPU or a smaller/non-thinking model — decision pending.
5. **Probabilistic metrics only where a predictive distribution exists**: PICP (80% interval) and CRPS (Gaussian closed form) for the fresh dcfootprint models; the Co-RE cache holds point forecasts only, so PICP/CRPS are blank there — not estimated.
6. **No water forecast for the US/EU** — no US/EU water time series exists in the project. Water appears only for Co-RE's 24 G3P basins (cached).

## Fresh dcfootprint SARIMA: fit validity (found and fixed during this run)

76 of the SARIMA fits are recorded failures and excluded (never scored as zero or clipped):

- 8 x LinAlgError: LU decomposition error.
- 20 x RuntimeError: MLE did not converge in 500 iterations
- 48 x RuntimeError: degenerate fit (coefficient on the unit boundary or non-finite SE)

Found by investigating implausible metrics, not by tuning: a non-converged Germany fit forecast an oscillating 225,000 GWh/month (actual ~45,000); a 'converged' Texas fit sat on the unit boundary (all coefficients = +-1, log-likelihood 0) and forecast 0 GWh. Fixes: MLE must converge (maxiter 500), coefficients off the unit boundary, finite SEs, missing months kept as NaN instead of dropped.
